title: Interaction of cells in the periodontal ligament during orthodontic tooth movement
summary:
The extent and speed of orthodontic tooth movement (OTM) vary between patients, as do the occurrence and extent of undesirable side effects.
The mechanisms of action of OTM have not yet been sufficiently researched. Orthodontic forces cause an inflammatory reaction in the tissue surrounding the tooth, which occurs without pathogens and ultimately results in bone remodelling in the direction of tooth movement. Many different cells and molecules are involved in this process, such as bone-modulating and immune cells. 
However, the interaction of immune cells with other cells during OTM requires further clarification, as only a few, sometimes contradictory findings are available. Furthermore, these studies are often not clinical studies involving patients. In general, T cells, which are immune cells, can be activated not only by biochemical signals but also mechanically. Their importance for OTM can be assumed, as, for example, the extent of OTM was reduced in mice without T cells.
The aim of this longitudinal and cross-sectional study is to investigate the activity of immune cells at different stages of orthodontic treatment. To this end, certain signalling proteins (cytokines) in a fluid located between the tooth and the surrounding gum (gingival crevicular fluid, GCF) will be examined. In addition, the presence of immune cells and, if applicable, their activity will be analysed.
 To this end, the analysis of cytokines and immune cells from the GCF and, if necessary, the determination of the activity of the immune cells is planned. The study will be divided into two parts: in the first part, the influence of time on cytokines and existing immune cells will be investigated in relatively similar patients. In the second part, patient- and therapy-specific factors will be evaluated using many different patients. Subsequently, statistical analysis will provide information about possible correlations between the immune cells present and their specific cytokines and the differences in OTM observed between different patients. This study aims to optimise orthodontic diagnosis and treatment.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Upper jaw: complete permanent dentition up to and including the first molars (part 1), permanent incisors (part 2)
- Lower jaw: permanent incisors
- Patients <22 years of age (part 1) or without upper age limit (part 2), provided that certain permanent teeth are present (see above). In accordance with physiological eruption times, this corresponds to a minimum age of 12 ± 1 years in Part 1 and 8 ± 1 years in Part 2.
- Patients of any gender
- Good oral health (approximal plaque index API ≤ 40%)
- No inflammatory processes such as gingivitis, periodontitis or abscesses (probing depth ≤ 3 mm, no radiologically detectable bone loss)
- Pre-therapeutic clinical diagnostics available (medical history, jaw models, OPG)
Exclusion criteria:
- Smoking
- Use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) during the last month or antibiotics during the last 3 months prior to and during orthodontic treatment
- Previous or current craniofacial fractures, craniofacial syndromes/anomalies, including cleft lip, jaw and palate
- Untreated carious lesions
-  Autoimmune diseases
